messages:
sara: noticed high east-west latency and repeated gRPC connection failures between gpu-worker pods in cluster-a. spikes started ~08:10 UTC, looks like inter-pod traffic is flapping. anyone seeing this?

mike: seeing same, pods on different nodes in the gpu-pool can't complete the RDMA handshake. metric: p99 latency jumped from 8ms to 350ms and retransmits increased.

jun: can you paste an example error?

sara: logs: `2026-03-18T08:12:03Z grpc: connection error: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport: connection lost` also `ibv_post_send` timeouts on some pods.

elaine: this smells like east-west blocked at network policy level. did we roll any netpols to gpu namespaces overnight?

mike: I just checked `kubectl get networkpolicy -n gpu-pool` — there is a new policy `egress-restrict-2026-03-18` applied at 07:58.

jun: paste `kubectl describe` please.

mike: `kubectl describe networkpolicy egress-restrict-2026-03-18 -n gpu-pool` output:

```
Name:         egress-restrict-2026-03-18
Namespace:    gpu-pool
PodSelector:  matchLabels: {}
PolicyTypes:  Egress
Egress:
  To:
    namespaceSelector:
      matchLabels:
        team: gpu-ops
  Ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

mike: the intent was to allow talk to the gpu-control namespace, but the control namespace is labeled `team: gpu-control` not `gpu-ops`. so the allowed namespaceSelector matches nothing.

sara: ahhhhh that would cause default-deny egress to block pod-to-pod traffic between namespaces (RDMA/mgmt uses a mix of TCP+UDP and ephemeral ports).

elaine: confirmation: `kubectl get ns --show-labels | grep gpu` shows `gpu-pool  team=gpu-pool` and `gpu-control  team=gpu-control`. no `gpu-ops`.

jun: quick workaround: add a permissive egress rule to allow cluster-internal pod CIDRs until we fix labels. Run: 

```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: tmp-allow-cluster-internal-egress
  namespace: gpu-pool
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/8
EOF
```

elaine: fine with me, do it and then we'll patch the original policy.

mike: applied `tmp-allow-cluster-internal-egress` at 08:25. RTTs dropped back to baseline within 2 mins. RDMA handshakes resumed.

sara: thanks. for root-cause we should fix `egress-restrict-2026-03-18` to use `team: gpu-control` or better use `namespaceSelector: matchLabels: role: control-plane` (more explicit). who wants to own the patch?

jun: I'll own it. plan: update the existing NetworkPolicy instead of deleting it. patch: 

```
kubectl patch networkpolicy egress-restrict-2026-03-18 -n gpu-pool --type='json' -p='[
  {"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/egress/0/to/0/namespaceSelector/matchLabels/team", "value": "gpu-control"}
]'
```

jun: then remove the tmp rule once stable. will also add a unit test to our k8s-policy CI to validate label existence before applying.

elaine: add a line in the deploy checklist to `kubectl get ns --show-labels` before netpol apply so this doesn't slip.

sara: can we also add a deploy-bot hook to reject netpol PRs that reference namespace labels that don't exist?

deploy-bot: automation idea logged: infra/terraform#412 (PR gate for netpol namespace labels). I'll post a short RFC. :robot_face:

mike: note for postmortem: impact was ~45min of degraded RPCs across production batch jobs; some retried and caused a small launch of extra pods -> marginally increased GPU spend for the hour.

jun: I've opened a short postmortem draft in `#incidents` and will paste a summary once I finish. will include command to grep for risky netpol diffs.

sara: awesome. resolved for now. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
